title: Unique Paths
description: A robot sits in the top-left cell of an `m x n` grid. It can only move **right** or **down** by one cell per move. Return the number of distinct routes to the bottom-right cell.
constraints: The answer is guaranteed to be at most 2 * 10^9
hints: The number of ways to reach a cell depends only on its neighbours above and to the left.
paths[r][c] = paths[r-1][c] + paths[r][c-1], with the first row and column all 1s.
You only need the previous row, so one array of length n suffices (the closed form C(m+n-2, m-1) also works).

solution.explanation: A cell can only be entered from above or from the left, so its path count is the sum of those two cells' counts. Sweeping row by row, a single array of length n holds the current row: row[c] += row[c-1]. That is O(m*n) time and O(n) space. Alternatively every route is a choice of which m-1 of the m+n-2 moves go down. Naive recursion is exponential.
